macro.headline: Bull regime intact but leadership rotates away from tech into cyclicals and healthcare.
macro.story:
The facts first: SPY closed at 751.28, up 3.1% over five days and sitting above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, with RSI at 58.1 and MACD holding above signal. The Dow is the standout — RSI 71.4 and +4.7% over 21 days — while QQQ has lagged (-2.8% over 21 days, MACD still below signal). VIX has cooled to 15.82, down more than 10% over the past week, and the term structure remains in contango. On the commodity side, WTI oil is deeply oversold (RSI 30, -25.8% over 21 days), gold and silver are below both moving averages, and the dollar is grinding higher (DXY +1.5% over 21 days). The 10-year yield is at 4.49% and the 2s10s curve has flattened to 0.35. Breadth stands at 46.6% bullish vs 25.1% bearish across the S&P 500, with 9 of 11 GICS sectors above their 50-day.

The tracked conversation offers a split explanation. The prevailing sentiment leans bullish on the AI complex — one thread frames the recent tech dip as an overreaction to recycled META compute news and a co-packaged optics delay, pointing to specific mega-cap semis and infrastructure names as the setup. That is consistent with QQQ stabilising (+2.3% over five days) but conflicts with the sector data, where Technology sits at a neutral/weak score of 4.2 with a bearish MACD — the narrative may be running ahead of the actual rotation. In parallel, a distinctly bearish strand of the conversation is flagging structural stress: small-cap interest expense running at 31% of EBITDA in the Russell 2000, a record wave of BDC redemption requests in private credit, foreign official Treasury holdings at a 27-year low, and Fed cut odds for 2026 collapsing from 85% to 21%. There is also chatter of a Strait of Hormuz shipping incident, though the WTI tape is not confirming any supply-shock premium — crude remains pinned near oversold lows. The bullish sentiment is aligned with the index tape; the bearish sentiment is aligned with what the credit and rates data are quietly showing underneath.

Sector work reinforces the message that leadership has shifted. Healthcare, Industrials, Materials, Financials and Utilities are all HOT with bullish MACDs, while Technology and Real Estate are neutral-to-weak and Energy is outright bearish (RSI 36, below its 50-day). This is a classic mid-cycle rotation profile — cyclicals and defensives leading together, growth digesting. The Early-Runway rotation signal is validated in Health Information Services, Diagnostics & Research, Credit Services, and Travel Services, all early in their hot spells with top-decile relative strength.

Forward watch: the tension to resolve is whether the QQQ/MACD divergence heals (bullish continuation) or whether the Dow's RSI-71 leadership tips over into a broader digestion. Rising 10-year yields, the DXY grind higher, and the credit-stress commentary are the tail risks worth respecting; the falling VIX, broad sector participation and validated rotation setups are the tailwind.

Oil at $69 with RSI 30.7 is in a downtrend, not a mean-reversion setup — the WTI oversold edge is negative.

That is exit-management territory, not a new-entry zone, and 21d is already -15.3% even as the trajectory holds bullish.
